title: Review of Ethnic Integration Policy for HDB Blocks and Neighbourhoods
what_it_is: Review of Ethnic Integration Policy for HDB Blocks and Neighbourhoods

sections.label: Questions on Ethnic Integration Policy
sections.summary: Questions ask whether the Ethnic Integration Policy is still necessary and whether it will be reviewed or its proportions adjusted.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Ethnic Integration Policy is still necessary in today’s context; and (b) if so, what steps are taken to assist minority sellers who may have difficulty in selling their HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development in view of the increasing number of inter-racial marriages and the changing profile of our households, whether the Ministry will consider (i) reviewing the Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) and (ii) adjusting EIP proportions for blocks and neighbourhoods.

sections.label: Introduction of EIP 1989
sections.summary: The EIP was introduced in 1989 for new and resale flats to prevent ethnic enclaves and keep public housing inclusive and diverse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We could see that, without intervention, there would, over time, once again, be ethnic enclaves which would separate us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: That is why we introduced the EIP in 1989, for both new as well as resale flats, to ensure that public housing estates remained inclusive and diverse, even beyond initial flat allocation.

sections.label: EIP limits reached
sections.summary: Nearly one in three HDB blocks and 14% of neighbourhoods have reached one or more EIP limits, persistently in some areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Today, nearly one out of every three HDB blocks, and 14% of HDB neighbourhoods, have reached one or more of the EIP limits, which means they have hit that particular ethnic limit more than the national proportion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In some areas, like Bukit Merah, Pasir Ris and Woodlands, the limits have been reached persistently across time.

sections.label: EIP remains relevant and necessary
sections.summary: The EIP remains relevant and necessary today as one important part of fostering racial harmony and inclusive neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And how much harder would it be for our children to correct their conscious and unconscious racial biases and learn how to live in a multicultural society?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, to Miss Cheryl Chan’s questions, yes, the EIP remains relevant and necessary today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Fostering real racial harmony is challenging and the EIP is one very important part of the solution because it helps to ensure inclusive and diverse neighbourhoods.

sections.label: EIP critical for homes and neighbourhoods
sections.summary: The EIP remains critical because much of life revolves around homes and neighbourhoods, despite other integration avenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Others also argue that there are other ways to mix and achieve social integration – in schools, at work or during National Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But the EIP remains critical because so much of our lives and our children's lives revolve around our homes and our neighbourhoods.

sections.label: REACH survey on racial quotas
sections.summary: A recent REACH survey found more than 60% of Singaporeans agreed racial quotas in public housing promote racial integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Based on a recent REACH survey, more than 60% of Singaporeans agreed that implementing racial quotas in public housing was an important way of promoting racial integration.

sections.label: HDB EIP waiver appeals
sections.summary: In 2020, HDB received about 500 EIP waiver appeals, roughly 2% of 23,100 resale applications filed that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2020, HDB received about 500 appeals for a waiver of the EIP, which is about 2% of the 23,100 resale applications filed last year.

sections.label: Successful EIP appeal percentage
sections.summary: The percentage of successful EIP-related appeals rose from 14% in 2018 to 21% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, the percentage of successful EIP-related appeals has risen from 14% in 2018 to 21% in 2020.
